reuse.why: The new range handler and existing consumers reuse recurConfigToRSchedule and applyWeekendRule, with holiday matching centralized in shared helpers.

duplication.why: Occurrence lookahead sizing is independently implemented in getNextDate and getUpcomingDates instead of sharing the policy for collecting retained occurrences.

placement.why: Adjustment rules remain in shared/schedules.ts and handler registration follows existing conventions, but server handlers now carry assumptions about those shared rules.

scope.why: The changes are focused on the requested scheduling rules, range handler, affected consumers, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The centralized adjustment function is clear, but independently maintained lookahead and padding formulas couple several consumers to the details of weekend and holiday handling.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All changed consumers apply the adjustment policy through applyWeekendRule.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate and server/schedules/app.ts:getUpcomingDates express the same retained-occurrence lookahead policy through differently shaped arithmetic.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains frequency and holidays, and applyWeekendRule gains a daily-frequency skip branch; all changed adjustment call sites still use it.
